intended_object: A dissection of a planar region X into polygons (here simplices given by vertex tuples): X is the union of the closed convex hulls of the pieces, and distinct pieces have disjoint interiors (open hulls). This is the notion used in Monsky's theorem on equal-area triangulations of the square. Inferred from the docstring, the module and its use in `isEqualAreaCover`.
explanation:
The definition is the conjunction of two conditions. `isCover X S` says X = ⋃_{P∈S} closedHull P. `isDisjointPolygonSet S` says that distinct P₁ ≠ P₂ in S have disjoint `openHull`s. `openHull` is the image of the open simplex under the barycentric-combination map, so for a nondegenerate triangle it is the interior. Together the two conditions are exactly the usual notion of a dissection (a cover by closed pieces with pairwise disjoint interiors), which is what Monsky's theorem needs.

One detail: pieces are vertex tuples, so two different tuples describing the same triangle (for example, a permutation of the vertices) count as distinct and would break disjointness. That only rules out listing a piece twice, which is the intended behaviour.

The setting is restricted to ℝ², but that is the setting of the whole Monsky development (the theorem is planar, and `openHull`/`closedHull` are defined there on ℝ²), so it does not make the definition too narrow. Mathlib has no dissection or tiling-cover notion that this duplicates.
